title: Double Dissociation Detective
summary: Four fictional case files, each score read against its own control group. A single dissociation leaves the rival explanation standing, a second person with the same pattern leaves it standing too, and only a reversal rules it out. A test-length control then shows that the same four percentages can be a double dissociation or no evidence at all.
learningObjectives: Explain why raw percentages on two different tasks are not comparable, and read each score against its own control group instead.
State the rival explanation a single dissociation cannot rule out, and say why a second person with the same pattern does not rule it out either.
Explain why a crossover rules that rival out, and what a double dissociation therefore establishes.
Judge whether a difference is larger than measurement error before classifying it.
Recognise that a double dissociation establishes at least partly separable processing, not where that processing sits.
interactionTypes: staged case files that accumulate evidence
control-referenced interval plot redrawn for every file
verdict classification against a fixed four-way scheme
live test-length control that changes the supported verdict
data table carrying every plotted value
privacy: Nothing is collected, stored or transmitted. All processing happens in the browser and no responses persist after the page is closed.
accessibilityNotes: Keyboard operable throughout. Answered verdicts are marked aria-disabled rather than disabled, so they stay in the tab order and can be re-read. The interval plot distinguishes a score whose whole interval clears the control range by a filled rather than hollow marker, so nothing depends on colour, and the shaded control band is dashed so its edge is visible at low contrast. Every plotted value appears in a data table beneath the plot, and the plot carries a description that is rewritten for each file. The test-length slider is a native range input paired with an output. Verdict changes are announced through a polite live region. No timed content and no motion.
dataStatus: Fictional cases. Every person, task, score, control mean and control standard deviation is invented for teaching. No figure is a norm, a prevalence or a published value, and no real patient or study is described.
simulationNotes: Scores are referenced to their own control group as z = (score - controlMean) / controlSd. Precision follows a binomial standard error, sqrt(p(1-p)/n), expressed in control units, and a difference counts as resolvable when it exceeds 1.96 standard errors. Classification follows the logic of the inference rather than the size of the gap. Three simplifications are carried over from the original: the observed proportion is held fixed while test length varies, so the slider isolates precision; control mean and standard deviation are treated as known exactly, where a single-case comparison properly uses a modified t test giving wider intervals; and the binomial standard error assumes items are independent and equally difficult.
readmeTopic: dissociation logic, control-referenced inference and what measurement precision entitles you to claim
